## Findings ledger
- [D2.DOC1.F8] The proposed transformation of technology supports the claim that political emancipation must alter the work process and technical ensemble rather than merely change who controls existing instruments — dim: argumentative_roles — term: political transformation of technology — role: premise: existing technology mutilates and subordinates workers; mechanism: workers and technical staff jointly redesign production; result: work can become a field of collective creativity — supports: a socialist transformation requires “a conscious transformation of technology” — anchor: "would imply a conscious transformation of technology on the part of the workers under conditions of workers’ management of production" — doc: technique — confidence: high — trimmed-anchor: yes

sections_inspected: Technique, creation and the constitution of the human world
scope_outcomes.criterion: Trace the move made with a concept and its warrant, distinguishing shared nouns from shared inferential roles.
scope_outcomes.basis: The inspected passages explicitly connect technique and related concepts to premises, mechanisms and conclusions concerning creation, social constitution, neutrality, determinism and political transformation.
limitations: The assessment concerns the supplied text and the stated sections only.

evidence_state.coverage_basis: reader/reviewer report; source bytes do not establish inspection or completeness
blocking_issues: One or more declared finding references lack retained verified evidence
